record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports qualitative ablation experiments on Qwen3-14B that bear on refusal-direction effects, but the method differs from the original global ablation: it mainly removes layer-local representations and reports qualitative generations.
record.gate_note: The README reports an experiment log for ablations and describes resulting refusal or response-policy behavior. The reported difference-of-means norm is not included as a row because the README says it does not imply a better refusal direction. The README also describes proposed experiments and files, which are not results.
record.test_reason: The study adapts the refusal-direction ablation to Qwen3-14B, using a paired-prompt per-layer SVD direction and a layer-20-only reference difference-of-means direction. It reports qualitative refusal and response-policy outcomes on 8 held-out prompts, so its own results bear on V1. It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a layer-20 rank-1 paired feature is behaviorally influential for their corpus but does not establish a universal Qwen3 refusal direction. They also say the original global AdvBench-vs-Alpaca recipe was too blunt on Qwen3-14B, and that the reference direction is less specific and less consistent than the paired one. They call the work exploratory and not publication-ready.
record.recipe_differences: The reference-data run uses an unpaired harmful-versus-harmless difference-of-means direction, but applies it only at selected layers rather than globally. The paired runs use matched prompts and layer-local SVD representations. This is an exploratory replication and mechanistic case study, not an exact reproduction of the original intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with layer band and rank; the README also distinguishes paired from reference data sources.
record.problems: One model and eight qualitative held-out prompts are reported. No independent benchmark, formal refusal rubric or quantitative refusal metric, benign-retention evaluation, placebo control, or statistical uncertainty estimates are reported. The README itself says the starter pairs share recurring wording and categories and that the paired and reference directions were not tested on the same external held-out set. Fluency is assessed qualitatively.

untested.parts: Adding or steering the direction to induce refusal: steer commands are shown but no results are reported. Quantitative refusal rate, benign retention and capability evaluation are also untested.
No weight edit; the interventions are inference-time hooks only.
No jailbreaks and no adversarial training.
No causal comparison of single versus multi-dimensional refusal mechanisms. The rank-4 run also changed the layer span. Only an SVD energy-concentration figure is reported.
Harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are not separated.
No transfer across languages, variants, or base and instruct models.

missing.what: The original global all-layer difference-of-means ablation on Qwen3-14B either had little targeted effect or damaged generation, causing degenerate repetition. This is stated qualitatively, with no row.
missing.locator: README intro paragraph; Reference-data comparison, last paragraph

missing.what: The first SVD component held roughly 83-87% of paired-difference energy at layers 20-25. This is geometric evidence of one dominant direction.
missing.locator: README, Experiment log, paragraph after table

record.verdict_notes: All evidence is qualitative: 8 prompts, no refusal rubric, no controls, no uncertainty. The file list (authpar/, scripts for patching, stats and a judge) suggests a larger pipeline whose results are not reported in the README. The record's V4 links and labels are removed: the rank-4 run confounds rank with layer span and measures only fluency. The record's V1 'challenges' label on r5 and r8 is folded into limits_scope, because layer-local ablation at non-causal layers is a layer-choice dependence, not a failure of the direction.

versions.untested_parts: No addition intervention is reported; ablation is at selected layers rather than every layer. Benign retention and general capability are not evaluated with a separate task or quantitative metric.
No weight edit is reported; the README says the interventions are reversible inference-time hooks and no weights are edited or saved.
No jailbreak attack or training against ablation is evaluated.
The README compares rank-one and rank-four SVD interventions, but does not compare affine or cone models, or establish whether multiple independent directions mediate refusal.
The study does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
It tests directions extracted within Qwen3-14B, not transfer of a direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No refusal-training method or training stage is varied.
The experiments deliberately disable thinking mode; reasoning-model behavior is not tested.

tranche.reason: It uses a different method (paired per-layer SVD direction, single-layer ablation) on the same question of whether ablating a refusal direction removes refusal. The global-recipe remark adds a T5-like argument but is secondary.

source_check.notes: The study text is a README only: one model, 8 held-out prompts, qualitative, no refusal counts, no random-direction control, no benign-retention test. So the call's capability=y overstates; only fluency is reported. The global original-recipe result has no row and should be added to missing. r2–r8 use the default paired corpus (48 of 56 starter pairs extracted, 8 held out). The paired direction is the top SVD vector of paired differences, not a plain difference-of-means. The README warns that several baseline generations were already educational rather than clean refusals.

statements.correction: README: the global unpaired difference-of-means recipe on Qwen3-14B 'either had little targeted effect or damaged generation quality'. Broad same-vector multi-layer ablation caused degenerate repetition. Paired rank-1 SVD direction ablated at layer 20 only: 'strong, fluent effects', qualitative, 8 held-out prompts, no rates. Reference AdvBench-vs-Alpaca difference-of-means at layer 20 only: mixed, several prompts still refused.
statements.problem: 'Layer-local rank-1 ablation at layer 20 worked' does not say which direction. Only the paired SVD direction gave strong effects. The AdvBench-vs-Alpaca difference-of-means direction at layer 20 was mixed. 'Worked' is also stronger than the README's qualitative wording.

statements.correction: Paired rank-1 SVD ablation on Qwen3-14B, non-thinking mode, 8 held-out prompts, qualitative. Layer 21 alone: near-baseline, direct refusals remained. Layers 22–23: refusals mostly remained, sometimes more explicit. Layers 22–24: weak, inconsistent changes. Layers 24–25: smaller, mixed. Layer 20 alone: strong, fluent effects; README calls it 'the dominant causal site'.
statements.problem: 'Layers 21–24' misreads the half-open ranges. Refusals mostly remained only at 22:24 (layers 22–23) and at layer 21 alone. Layers 22–24 gave weak, inconsistent changes; 24–25 gave smaller, mixed effects. The statement also leaves out that layer-20 ablation gave strong effects, so this is layer dependence, not a failure of removal on Qwen3-14B.

statements.correction: README: the global difference-of-means vector 'either had little targeted effect or damaged generation quality'. The first SVD component held about 83–87% of paired-difference energy at layers 20–25, so rank 1 was preferred over rank 4. A rank-1 paired direction at layer 20 alone gave strong, fluent effects (qualitative, 8 prompts). The study bears on global vs layer-local application and on unpaired extraction, not on needing more than one direction.
statements.problem: It cites this study as evidence that one direction is insufficient. In fact this study prefers a single rank-1 direction at one layer, which gave strong effects. Its objection is to applying one unpaired vector globally across layers. The statement also drops the 'or damaged generation quality' alternative.
